description: Width tiers for Dance — Years 5-6 band
subject: Dance

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest single task context that honestly meets the descriptor's command term. For Y5-6 Dance, minimum requires demonstrable choreographic device use, technical-expressive skill application, or analytical comparison.
width_notes.typical_width: Full descriptor scope from elaborations — covers device use, technical/expressive skill development, cultural comparison and First Nations inquiry as ACARA intended for this band.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment adding new task contexts, genre/style explorations, cultural investigations or extended reflective practice. First Nations elaborations in wider throughout.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data. Y5-6 introduces choreographic devices and formal performance contexts.

AC9ADA6C01.minimum_width: Manipulate at least two elements of dance and apply at least one choreographic device to structure a dance communicating a clear idea — with a section structure using the device.
AC9ADA6C01.typical_width: Manipulate elements and apply choreographic devices (repetition, contrast, unison, alternating sections) to choreograph dances across multiple stimuli and purposes: narrative dances retelling stories, thematic dances exploring issues, dances with technical-expressive focus; refine using Viewpoints; consider production elements.
wider: Choreograph a dance that takes a position on a sustainability or social issue — using device and structural choices to build a narrative or argument arc
Use production elements (music, costume, props) as co-compositional tools — exploring how production choices shape what and how the dance communicates
Investigate element and device use in a dance from an unfamiliar cultural context and apply one observed technique in own choreography — noting what changes in the communicative effect
elaborations: exploring character and mood by experimenting with elements, developing narrative dance
devising movement possibilities and selecting, combining, arranging and refining; using some movements in repeating sections that alternate with contrasting sections
creating dance that focuses on technical and expressive skills
creating dance that explores a theme or issue such as sustainability

AC9ADA6D01.minimum_width: Refine technical execution of at least two movement types with targeted practice; demonstrate at least two expressive skills in a performance context.
AC9ADA6D01.typical_width: Develop and practise technical and expressive skills: refining galloping, jumping, sliding, rolling, spinning, shrinking, exploding, collapsing; developing focus, clarity, confidence and facial expression/character; improvising in response to stimuli; exploring positive and negative space and contrasting dynamics; applying safe dance practice throughout.
wider: Sustain technical development focus on one demanding movement type across multiple sessions — setting quality benchmarks and tracking improvement over time
Use video self-review to identify expressive skill strengths and development areas — setting a specific goal for a subsequent performance
Explore how the same technical skill (e.g. jumping) is executed in two different dance styles — developing style-aware technical range
elaborations: improvising new movement to communicate ideas in response to stimulus
developing technical and expressive skills to refine execution of fundamental movements
developing expressive skills of focus, clarity of movement, confidence and facial expression/character
exploring an element of dance; experimenting with shapes and positive/negative space, contrasting dynamics

AC9ADA6E01.minimum_width: Identify how at least two elements combine in one observed dance to create a specific communicative effect; describe the purpose and mood created.
AC9ADA6E01.typical_width: Explore how elements are combined across dances from different cultures, times and places to communicate ideas: using Viewpoints to explore similarities and differences; discussing purpose of movements, elements, production elements and their effect on mood and audience; seeking feedback on own choreographic intent; examining how dance communicates cultural traditions.
wider: Investigate how dance-on-screen (film, music video) uses production elements alongside dance elements — examining how the combination changes what is communicated compared with live performance
Explore how a dance from a country or region in Asia uses elements in ways that differ from familiar Western dance styles — discussing what this reveals about cultural values, aesthetics and purpose
Investigate how dance styles from popular culture reflect the cultural and historical moment in which they emerged
elaborations: exploring how dances use elements and choreographic devices such as repetition, unison, contrast
seeking feedback about how audience interpreted the dance's movements
discussing purpose of movements, elements, production elements and technical/expressive skills and their effect on mood
asking Viewpoints questions to explore similarities and differences across choreographers
exploring how dance communicates cultural traditions; considering dances from Asia

AC9ADA6E02.minimum_width: Describe one way that dance helps First Nations Australians continue or revitalise a specific cultural practice; explain why this matters using a concrete example.
AC9ADA6E02.typical_width: Explore how and why cultural expressions are critical for sharing, continuing and revitalising First Nations Australian cultures; investigate meaning and purpose in dance at community events; experience how First Nations Australians' stories communicate connection to Country/Place; use Viewpoints to build inquiry questions; explore how narrative dances maintain culture.
wider: Investigate how narrative dances communicate knowledge about sustainable approaches to locating and gathering food, or stories about how places got their names
Compare how two different First Nations Australian dance practices serve cultural continuation — noting what is community-specific versus what is more broadly shared
Develop and pursue a self-directed inquiry question about a First Nations Australian dance practice — using Viewpoints and co-created resources as inquiry tools
elaborations: exploring how and why cultural expressions are critical for sharing, continuing or revitalising cultures
investigating how meaning and purpose are communicated in dance at community events
experiencing how First Nations Australians' stories and ideas communicate connection to and responsibility for Country/Place
using Viewpoints to develop questions and build understanding about First Nations dance
exploring how narrative dances maintain culture — knowledge about sustainable practices or place stories

AC9ADA6P01.minimum_width: Perform one dance using at least two technical-expressive skills and at least one production element; reflect using one Viewpoints question identifying a strength and a development area.
AC9ADA6P01.typical_width: Practise and perform in informal and/or formal settings: applying technical and expressive skills to communicate ideas; using production elements (music, costume, props) to enhance different performance contexts; rehearsing with awareness of body capabilities; performing with cultural community representatives using traditional music; using Viewpoints to evaluate and refine.
wider: Perform for an audience beyond the class — a school assembly, community event, or online platform — developing performance presence and audience awareness across contexts

Perform a dance using traditional music with representatives of the relevant cultural community — following cultural protocols and discussing how the community context changes the performance experience
Develop and use a personal rehearsal strategy — setting improvement targets, using video review, and documenting progress across a rehearsal period
elaborations: rehearsing and performing with awareness of body capabilities and applying technical and expressive skills
using specific technical and expressive skills to communicate ideas, perspectives and meaning
presenting using production elements — music, costumes, props — appropriate to the context
using Viewpoints to reflect on performance — space, energy, relationship between dancers and audience
